title: Pilot study comparing different ways of wearing splints for guard awake bruxism
summary:
The aim of the study is to test two different ways of wearing a splint for the treatment of awake bruxism (teeth grinding and clenching during wakefulness). The aim of this study is to investigate whether both wearing methods lead to the same extent to a subjective and objective (verifiable by measured values) reduction in waking bruxism behaviour and muscular discomfort.
The following additional examinations are required of the patient as a result of the study:
Insertion of the splint:
- Questionnaire to assess the splint
Duration approx. 5 minutes
Follow-up appointment 1: after 4 weeks: 
- Brief examination for bruxism (bruxism screening)
- Questionnaire to assess the success of splint therapy
Duration approx. 15 minutes.
Follow-up appointment 2: after 3 months: 
- Brief examination for bruxism (bruxism screening)
- Clinical functional examination of the temporomandibular joints and masticatory muscles (clinical functional status and manual structural analysis)
- Psycho-social questionnaires
- Questionnaire to assess the splint
- Digital recording of muscle-guided mandibular movements (arrow angle registration)
- Scanning of the the success of splint therapy
Duration approx. 45 minutes.
Patients who have been diagnosed with a problem in the temporomandibular joint (e.g. malposition of the temporomandibular joint head in the socket) or an increase in the size of the masticatory muscle (lateral pterygoid muscle) during the initial MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) are referred for a follow-up MRI of the temporomandibular joint.

interventions.name:
Insertion of a splint for awake bruxism
Arm 1: Wearing the splint at night
Arm 2: Wearing the splint at night and 6 hours during the day

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
probable awake bruxism
Exclusion criteria:
lack of patient consent, secondary bruxism, suspected diagnosis of arthropathy, chronic pain GCPS >2, contraindication MRI, patients with dementia or other cognitive impairments who are unable to consent to the study, patients who do not consent to participate in the study for other reasons
